Emits a lint for a HIR node with an explicit span and caller-provided message/decorator closure. It calls `lint_level_at_node` and then forwards to `lint_level`.
Finds the crate-level attribute insertion point for a HIR node by walking parent nodes until the crate root is reached. It calls `hir`, `parent_iter`, and `shrink_to_lo`.

When running on nightly, augments a diagnostic with help or a crate-level `#![feature(...)]` suggestion for disabled features. It calls `is_nightly_build`, uses `crate_level_attribute_injection_span` via `and_then`, and then emits either `span_suggestion_verbose` or `help`.
Emits a lint for a HIR node using a `LintDiagnostic` decorator. It calls `node_lint`, passing the decorator’s `msg`, and invokes `decorate_lint` in the decoration closure.
Emits a lint for a HIR node without an explicit span, using the node’s computed lint level and a caller-provided decoration closure. It calls `lint_level_at_node` and then forwards to `lint_level`.

Maps a duplicated lifetime parameter from an opaque type back to the corresponding lifetime in the parent context, recursively climbing through nested opaques when necessary and reconstructing either an early- or late-bound region. It calls `def_kind`, `def_descr`, `to_def_id`, `local_parent`, `hir_node_by_def_id`, `named_bound_var`, `parent`, `generics_of`, `hir`, and `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, and constructs the final region with `new_early_param`, `new_late_param`, or an error region constructor.
Returns intrinsic metadata for a definition only if it is a function or associated function. It calls `def_kind` to filter eligible items and then `intrinsic_raw`.
Returns the stolen resolver-and-AST-lowering bundle used during lowering. It directly calls `resolver_for_lowering_raw` and extracts its resolver component.
Returns the trait reference implemented by an impl, if any. It calls `impl_trait_header` and extracts the `trait_ref` from the result.
Returns an impl’s polarity, defaulting to positive when no trait header exists. It calls `impl_trait_header` and uses its result to choose the polarity.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/coercion.r: Returns the wrapped `FnCtxt` reference so `Coerce` can transparently use `FnCtxt` APIs; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Checks whether coercion from one mutability to another is allowed, permitting weakening from mutable to immutable and rejecting strengthening; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Builds an empty adjustment list for coercions that need no HIR/MIR adjustment; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Creates a closure that wraps a single `Adjust` into a one-element adjustment list targeting the inferred type; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Packages adjustments, target type, and generated obligations into a successful `CoerceResult`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Constructs a `Coerce` helper with the given `FnCtxt`, obligation cause, and two-phase-borrow policy, initializing it in subtyping mode; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Performs the underlying type relation for coercion, using either LUB or supertype unification under a snapshot and, with the next solver, filtering out impossible obligations before succeeding; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Runs `unify` and, on success, converts the unified target type into adjustments and a final coercion result by calling `unify` and `success`.

Main coercion dispatcher: resolves shallow type vars, handles `!` to any, unresolved-source fallback, unsizing, pointer/reference/dyn-star coercions, function-item/fn-pointer/closure conversions, and otherwise falls back to unification. It explicitly calls `success`, `simple`, `coerce_from_inference_variable`, `coerce_unsized`, `coerce_unsafe_ptr`, `coerce_borrowed_pointer`, `coerce_dyn_star`, `coerce_from_fn_item`, `coerce_from_fn_pointer`, `coerce_closure_to_fn`, and `unify_and`.

Handles coercion when the source is an unresolved type variable: if both sides are unresolved it emits `Coerce` obligations toward a chosen target, otherwise it falls back to subtype/LUB unification by calling `unify_and`.

Implements coercions to borrowed references, including mutability checks, fallback when the source is not already a reference, and autoderef-plus-autoref reborrows that search for a matching referent. It explicitly calls `coerce_mutbls`, `unify_and`, `unify`, and `success`.

Attempts unsizing-based coercions after rejecting unresolved types, handling reborrows for references/raw pointers, creating the necessary pointer adjustments, and proving `Unsize`/`CoerceUnsized` obligations before returning. It explicitly calls `coerce_mutbls` and `unify_and`.

Implements coercion to `dyn*`: if source and target already have the same principal trait object it falls back to plain unification, otherwise it builds existential, outlives, and `PointerLike` obligations and emits a `DynStar` adjustment. It explicitly calls `unify_and`.

Shared helper for safe-function coercions that conditionally inserts a safe-to-unsafe fn-pointer conversion, otherwise performs normal unification, then leak-checks the snapshot before committing. It explicitly calls `unify_and`.

Handles coercion from a function pointer type, chiefly allowing safe-to-unsafe weakening through the shared helper. It explicitly calls `coerce_from_safe_fn`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for the non-adjusting path.

Handles coercion from a function item by normalizing the target, rejecting intrinsic and forbidden target-feature casts, reifying the item to a fn pointer when needed, and then delegating safe/unsafe function coercion; otherwise it falls back to plain unification. It explicitly calls `coerce_from_safe_fn`, `simple`, and `unify_and`.

Coerces a non-capturing closure to a function pointer by constructing the unclosed fn-pointer signature and unifying it with a closure-fn-pointer adjustment; capturing closures or non-fn-pointer targets fall back to plain unification. It explicitly calls `unify_and`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for the fallback path.

Implements coercion to raw pointers from references or other raw pointers, checking mutability compatibility and choosing between reborrow-style raw-pointer formation, mut-to-const weakening, or no-op pointer unification. It explicitly calls `unify_and`, `coerce_mutbls`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for fallback/no-op cases.

Top-level expression coercion entry point: resolves source/target types, builds a `Coerce` helper, runs coercion in a snapshot, registers resulting obligations, applies adjustments to the expression, and returns the coerced target or an error type. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::coerce`.

Predicate-style check for whether one type can coerce to another by probing a `Coerce` run and ensuring all produced obligations can be selected. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::coerce`.
Searches autoderef steps to find the first intermediate type that can unify with the target and returns that deref count. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::unify`.
Diagnostic helper that autodereferences once and returns the dereferenced type only if the original type may implement `DerefMut`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Computes a coercion-aware least upper bound across expressions, first trying ordinary LUB, then special-casing distinct function items and non-capturing closures by reifying them to compatible fn pointers and applying the resulting adjustments to prior coercion sites. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `FnCtxt::coerce`.
Convenience wrapper that creates a root type-checking context and `FnCtxt`, then asks that context whether `ty` can coerce to `output_ty`. It explicitly calls `FnCtxt::can_coerce`.
Constructs a `CoerceMany` accumulator with dynamic storage for coercion sites. It explicitly calls `CoerceMany::make`.
Constructs a `CoerceMany` accumulator using a pre-supplied slice of coercion sites. It explicitly calls `CoerceMany::make`.
Internal constructor that initializes the expected type, optional merged type, expression storage, and push count for `CoerceMany`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Returns the originally expected type tracked by the `CoerceMany` accumulator; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Returns the current merged/coerced type if one has been established, otherwise the initial expected type; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Adds one expression to the multi-expression coercion process by delegating to the internal coercion driver. It explicitly calls `coerce_inner`.
Forces the next coerced value to have type `()`, delegating all work to `coerce_inner` with the unit type and no expression node.

Performs the main multi-expression coercion step: resolves inference variables, propagates prior error types, chooses expected/found types for diagnostics, then either coerces the first expression with `fcx.coerce` or merges later expressions with `fcx.try_find_coercion_lub`. On success it updates the merged type, registers obligations, and records the coercion site via `as_coercion_site`; on failure it builds diagnostics, including calling `report_return_mismatched_types`, `is_return_ty_definitely_unsized`, and `suggest_boxing_tail_for_return_position_impl_trait` when applicable.

Checks whether both candidate tail-expression types satisfy the return-position `impl Trait` bounds, and if so emits diagnostics suggesting boxing. It probes compatibility by creating an obligation context and calling `register_obligations` and `select_where_possible`.

Builds a detailed diagnostic for return-position coercion failures. It starts with `fcx.err_ctxt().report_mismatched_types`, then adds targeted suggestions such as `suggest_missing_semicolon`, `suggest_mismatched_types_on_tail`, `suggest_semicolon_at_end`, `suggest_missing_return_type`, and `suggest_missing_break_or_return_expr` based on the surrounding HIR context.

Determines whether the enclosing function's return type is definitely not `Sized`. It calls `body_fn_sig` to get the function signature and `predicate_may_hold` on a constructed `Sized` obligation over `sig.output()`.
Finishes coercion accumulation by returning the computed final type if one exists, or `!` when no non-never inputs were successfully pushed.
Trait requirement that returns the HIR expression to use as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns the expression itself as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Forwards coercion-site lookup through a shared reference by calling `as_coercion_site` on the underlying `T`.
Unreachable implementation for the never type that returns `*self` as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Uses a match arm's body expression as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/closure.rs: Entry point for type-checking a closure expression. It derives an optional expected signature and closure kind from the surrounding expectation by calling `deduce_closure_signature` after resolving the expected type, fetches the closure body from HIR, and then delegates actual closure checking to `check_closure`.

Attempts to infer an expected closure signature and closure kind from an expected type. Depending on the expected type form, it calls `deduce_closure_signature_from_predicates` for opaque types and inference variables, calls `deduce_sig_from_projection` when analyzing trait-object projection bounds, and directly recognizes function pointers as `Fn` closures.

Scans elaborated self-predicates to infer a closure signature and the most restrictive callable kind. For projection predicates, it calls `deduce_sig_from_projection` and normalizes the result, then filters out self-referential inferred signatures using the local `MentionsTy::visit_ty` visitor; it also derives closure kind information from encountered Fn-trait predicates.

Visitor helper used to detect whether an inferred signature mentions the expected self type. It returns a break when the visited type equals the tracked expected type; otherwise it continues traversal with `super_visit_with`.

Extracts an expected function signature from a projection predicate on an `Fn*` trait or coroutine `Return` associated type. It validates that the projection comes from a supported trait, resolves tuple inputs and return type, and constructs the resulting `ExpectedSig`.

Chooses how to compute a closure signature based on whether an expectation is available. It calls `sig_of_closure_with_expectation` when an expected signature exists, otherwise it calls `sig_of_closure_no_expectation`.

Computes closure signatures without contextual expectations. It calls `supplied_sig_of_closure` to obtain the user-declared or inferred poly-signature, then calls `closure_sigs` to derive the bound and liberated forms.

Computes closure signatures while incorporating an expected signature from context. It falls back to `sig_of_closure_no_expectation` when variadics or arity do not match, calls `sig_of_closure_with_mismatched_number_of_arguments` for argument-count mismatches, builds contextual closure signatures with `closure_sigs`, and then calls `merge_supplied_sig_with_expectation`; on success it registers obligations, and on failure it again falls back to `sig_of_closure_no_expectation`.

Handles the case where the expected signature and closure declaration have different arities. It reports an argument-count error, calls `error_sig_of_closure` to manufacture an error signature, and then calls `closure_sigs` to produce the closure’s bound and liberated signatures from that error signature.

Attempts to unify the user-supplied closure signature with the expectation-derived signatures under inference. It calls `supplied_sig_of_closure`, instantiates fresh variables for supplied inputs, equates supplied and expected argument and return types, accumulates resulting obligations, and rebuilds the merged liberated signature for the returned `ClosureSignatures`.

Builds the polymorphic signature directly from the closure’s written parameter and return annotations, inserting inference variables where annotations are absent. For async function bodies with default return type, it calls `deduce_future_output_from_obligations` to recover the future output type; it then constructs, canonicalizes, caches, and normalizes the resulting `PolyFnSig`.

Infers the output type of an async function body by inspecting pending obligations or opaque-type bounds on the expected return type. It searches projection predicates via the local helper closure, which calls `deduce_future_output_from_projection`, then normalizes the discovered output type and replaces opaque types with inference variables before registering any resulting obligations.

Extracts the `Future::Output` type from a projection predicate. It rejects predicates with bound variables or projections from non-`Future` traits, verifies that the associated item is `Output`, resolves the projected term, and returns the projected type.

Constructs an error-marked closure signature after a prior diagnostic has been emitted. It still lowers any explicitly written parameter and return types for bookkeeping, but replaces all inputs and the output with an error type and returns that synthetic signature.

Converts a bound closure signature into the pair of signatures used by later closure checking. It liberates late-bound regions from the provided bound signature, normalizes the liberated form, and returns both as `ClosureSignatures`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/check.rs::: Type-checks a function body by preparing the `FnCtxt` state, replacing opaque return types with inference variables, forbidding invalid intrinsic ABIs, gathering locals, checking parameter patterns and well-formedness, enforcing sizedness constraints, checking the body, and reconciling the coerced body result with the declared return type; it explicitly calls `forbid_intrinsic_abi` and uses `GatherLocalsVisitor::new(...).visit_body(...)` to collect locals before parameter/body checking.

Validates that the panic handler lang item has the required non-generic function form by constructing the expected `for<'a, 'b> fn(&'a PanicInfo<'b>) -> !` signature and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to compare it against the actual signature.

Validates the `start` lang item signature by building the expected `fn(main: fn() -> T, argc: isize, argv: *const *const u8, sigpipe: u8) -> isize` form and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to enforce it.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/expr.rs::i: Checks an expression against a required type by calling `check_expr_with_expectation`, permits the special `!`-to-any adjustment via `apply_adjustments`, and then enforces the final subtype relation with `demand_suptype_diag`, adding mismatch suggestions before emitting any error.
Type-checks an expression with a type hint by calling `check_expr_with_hint`, then coerces the result to the expected type with `demand_coerce` without two-phase borrowing.
A thin helper that calls `check_expr_with_expectation` with `ExpectHasType(expected)` to type-check an expression using a concrete expected type as a hint.
Checks an expression by calling `check_expr_with_expectation`, and if the usage requires a mutable place, calls `convert_place_derefs_to_mutable` to upgrade deref adjustments accordingly.
Default expression entry point that calls `check_expr_with_expectation` with no expectation.
Checks an expression with place/mutability requirements by calling `check_expr_with_expectation_and_needs` with no type expectation.
Main convenience wrapper that forwards expression checking to `check_expr_with_expectation_and_args` with no call arguments or enclosing call expression.

Core expression-checking entry point that handles logging, unreachable-code and divergence bookkeeping, then dispatches path expressions to `check_expr_path` and all other expression forms to `check_expr_kind`, finally resolving the resulting type for recording and diagnostics.

Dispatches each HIR expression kind to its specialized checker, including `check_lit`, `check_binop`, `check_expr_assign`, `check_binop_assign`, `check_expr_unary`, `check_expr_addr_of`, `check_lang_item_path`, `check_expr_path`, `check_expr_asm`, `check_offset_of`, `check_expr_break`, `check_expr_return`, `check_expr_become`, `check_expr_let`, `check_expr_loop`, and `check_match`.

Checks a unary expression by first calling `check_expr_with_expectation` on the operand, then resolving and validating the operator: deref uses `lookup_derefing`, while `!` and `-` use `check_user_unop` with builtin-type fast paths.

Checks `&`/`&raw` expressions by deriving an operand hint from the expected pointer/reference type, calling `check_expr_with_expectation_and_needs` on the operand, and then either calling `check_named_place_expr` for raw borrows or creating a fresh region for shared/mutable references.
Validates that a raw-borrow operand is a named place expression, allowing adjusted deref-based places, and emits an `AddressOfTemporaryTaken` error otherwise.
Resolves a lang item path by calling `resolve_lang_item_path` and returning the resolved type component.

Checks a value path by resolving it with `resolve_ty_and_res_fully_qualified_call`, diagnosing bad resolutions with `suggest_assoc_method_call` or variant-specific reporting, and otherwise instantiating it via `instantiate_value_path`; for function definitions it also records deferred intrinsic/transmute and sized-parameter checks.

Checks a `break` expression by consulting the enclosing breakable context, type-checking any break value with `check_expr_with_hint`, and coercing it into the loop’s break accumulator while producing targeted diagnostics for illegal or mismatched break values.

Checks a `return` expression by calling `emit_return_outside_of_fn_body` when outside a function body, otherwise either type-checking the returned value with `check_return_expr` or forcing unit into the return coercion; when outside a function but a value is present, it still calls `check_expr` on that value for error recovery.

Checks an explicit tail-call `become` by obtaining the function return type, calling `check_expr_with_hint` on the callee expression, and enforcing it with `demand_suptype`; if used outside a function body, it calls `emit_return_outside_of_fn_body` and falls back to `check_expr` for recovery.

Checks a return value inside a function by reading the expected return type from the return coercion, calling `check_expr_with_hint` on the returned expression, coercing it into the function return via the return coercion, and then calling `select_obligations_where_possible` to reroute opaque-type errors through `point_at_return_for_opaque_ty_error` when needed.

Builds and emits a diagnostic for `return`/`become` used outside the current function body, enriching the error with enclosing function/body spans when the statement appears inside a nested body within a function item.
Rewrites fulfillment errors caused by `OpaqueReturnType(None)` so they point at the specific return expression span and type instead of a broader enclosing block span.

Validates that an assignment left-hand side is a syntactic place expression, and if not, produces a tailored diagnostic that may call `comes_from_while_condition` and `check_for_missing_semi` before applying caller-supplied error adjustments.
Detects the multiline `foo() *bar = baz` pattern that often means a missing semicolon and emits a semicolon insertion suggestion when appropriate.
Walks parent HIR nodes to determine whether an expression originated from a `while` condition and, if so, invokes the provided callback on that condition expression.

Checks an `if`/`if-else` by calling `check_expr_has_type_or_error` on the condition, `warn_if_unreachable` for the then-branch, `check_expr_with_expectation` on each branch, and then coercing branch types together with branch-specific diagnostics and divergence tracking.

Checks assignment expressions by computing the expected unit-like result, issuing `=` vs `==` diagnostics when boolean context suggests it, type-checking operands via `check_expr`, `check_expr_with_needs`, and `check_expr_with_hint`, enforcing RHS-to-LHS coercion with `demand_coerce_diag`, and validating assignability with `check_lhs_assignable`.
Checks a `let` expression by calling `warn_if_unreachable` on its initializer and `check_decl` with statement-style rules, then returns `bool` unless recovery marked the expression as erroneous.

Checks loop expressions by creating an optional break-value coercion target from the expectation, running the body through `with_breakable_ctxt` and `check_block_no_value`, updating divergence based on whether breaks occur, and completing the accumulated break coercion when present.

Checks a method call by calling `check_expr` on the receiver, resolving its type, looking up the method with `lookup_method`, recording successful resolution with `write_method_call_and_enforce_effects` or diagnosing failure with `report_method_error`, and then calling `check_method_argument_types`.

Checks a cast by lowering the target type, calling `check_expr_with_expectation` on the source with `ExpectCastableToType`, resolving both sides, and either returning an immediate error or deferring the detailed validation through `cast::CastCheck::new`.

Checks array literals by choosing an element coercion target from the expectation or a fresh type variable, calling `check_expr_with_hint` for each element, coercing them through a `CoerceMany`, then calling `suggest_array_len` and returning the resulting array type.

Looks up the enclosing typed array context for an expression and, when it finds an inferred array-length placeholder, emits a diagnostic suggesting the concrete `array_len`. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks a const block in a fresh `FnCtxt`: it gathers locals, checks the body against the given expectation, enforces that the resulting type is sized, records the block type, and returns it. This method calls the listed method `check_expr_with_expectation`.

Type-checks an array repeat expression `[element; count]` by lowering/evaluating the length, optionally suggesting an explicit array length, deriving the element type from the expected array/slice type when possible, checking the element, enforcing repeat-copy requirements, building the array type, and registering a well-formedness obligation. This method calls the listed methods `suggest_array_len`, `check_expr_coercible_to_type`, `check_expr_has_type_or_error`, and `check_repeat_element_needs_copy_bound`.

Determines whether a repeat-expression element must satisfy `Copy`, exempting true constants and const blocks, classifying const-call/const-constructor cases for diagnostics, and requiring the `Copy` lang-item obligation only when the evaluated repeat count may exceed 1. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks a tuple expression by extracting expected field types from an expected tuple when available, coercing matching elements to those types, otherwise checking elements with no expectation, assembling the tuple type, propagating error types, and requiring the tuple initializer to be sized. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr_coercible_to_type` and `check_expr_with_expectation`.

Type-checks a struct literal by resolving the struct path, recovering by checking subexpressions on path-resolution failure, rejecting external non-exhaustive struct construction, checking all provided/base fields, and requiring the resulting ADT type to be sized. This method calls the listed methods `check_struct_path`, `check_struct_fields_on_error`, and `check_expr_struct_fields`.

Checks the fields of a struct literal against the chosen variant: it reconciles expectation-derived hints with the ADT type, tracks remaining and duplicate fields, resolves each supplied field, records field indices, validates stability and field types, reports unknown fields, checks field expressions with hints/coercions, registers well-formedness obligations, and emits diagnostics for missing fields or FRU-related mistakes. This method calls the listed methods `expected_inputs_for_expected_output`, `demand_eqtype`, `write_field_index`, `field_ty`, `report_unknown_field`, `check_expr_with_hint`, `demand_coerce_diag`, and `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.
Performs error-recovery checking for struct literal contents by still type-checking every explicit field expression and the optional base expression. This method calls the listed method `check_expr`.

Builds and emits the missing-fields diagnostic for a struct literal, formatting a readable list of omitted fields and, when there is at least one written field, delegating to a FRU typo suggestion path before emission. This method calls the listed method `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.

Detects the common typo where a range literal was written where functional record update syntax was likely intended, attaches a targeted FRU subdiagnostic and suppresses conflicting range-type errors when applicable, otherwise emitting the original error directly. It does not call other listed methods.

Reports that a struct literal cannot be constructed because of private fields, distinguishing explicitly used versus merely remaining private fields, labeling or noting them, and searching inherent impl items for constructor-like associated functions whose signatures match the ADT so it can suggest alternatives. It does not call other listed methods.

Emits the diagnostic for using an unknown field in a struct/variant literal, tailoring the message for enum variants vs other ADTs, suggesting tuple-style constructor syntax for tuple variants, and offering likely field-name corrections based on available visible fields. This method calls the listed methods `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.

Collects suggestable field names from a variant, excluding fields already present in `skip_fields` and filtering through field-suggestability checks. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.
Formats a bounded, human-readable comma-separated series of field names, appending an `... and N others` suffix when the list is longer than the display limit. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks field access by checking and resolving the base expression, autodereferencing through candidate receiver types, locating direct or nested ADT fields, recording field indices, applying deref adjustments and obligations for accessible fields, handling tuple indexing syntax, and otherwise reporting private or nonexistent-field errors. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `find_adt_field`, `field_ty`, `write_field_index`, `ban_private_field_access`, and `ban_nonexisting_field`.

When the base type is an `impl Future`, checks whether the requested field exists on the future's `Output` type and, if so, suggests inserting `.await`; otherwise it just labels the field as unknown. It does not call other listed methods.

Builds and emits the main diagnostic for accessing a nonexistent field, specializing suggestions for arrays, raw pointers, type parameters, and opaque futures, then trying a method-call suggestion if calling the base expression would yield a type with the requested field, and adding the Rust-2018 `.await` note when relevant. This method calls the listed methods `no_such_field_err`, `maybe_suggest_array_indexing`, `suggest_first_deref_field`, `point_at_param_definition`, and `suggest_await_on_field_access`.

Emits the private-field-access diagnostic and, when appropriate, suggests calling an accessible method with the same name instead of reading the field. This method calls the listed method `private_field_err`.

Reports the error for treating a method as a field value, then suggests either removing wrapping parentheses for an accidental call pattern, adding call parentheses, or dereferencing first for raw-pointer-to-ADT cases where the field exists after dereference. It does not call other listed methods.

Augments a diagnostic for field access on a type parameter by locating the non-synthetic type parameter declaration in the current body and labeling where that parameter was introduced. It does not call other listed methods.

For mistaken tuple-style field syntax on arrays, labels the field as unknown and, when the field parses as an integer and the array length is evaluable, suggests rewriting `.n` as `[n]` with an applicability tuned by bounds confidence. It does not call other listed methods.
For raw-pointer field access, labels the field as unknown and suggests wrapping the base expression in an explicit dereference before accessing the field. It does not call other listed methods.

Constructs the base `no field` diagnostic and enriches it with suggestions for nested-field access paths, misspelled field names, and visible candidate field listings; it also unwraps `Option`/`Result`-like outer types when searching for nested matches. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy`, `check_for_nested_field_satisfying`, and `name_series_display`.
Constructs the base diagnostic for accessing a private field, naming the enclosing item and labeling the offending field span. It does not call other listed methods.

Autodereferences a base type and gathers visible, suggestable fields from non-enum ADTs, skipping wrappers whose fields are all private and capping the number of searched fields for compile-time cost. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.

Recursively searches through visible nested ADT fields up to depth three for a field satisfying the provided predicate, extending and returning the field path on success. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy` and `check_for_nested_field_satisfying` recursively.

Type-checks indexing expressions by checking both operands, resolving the base type, using normal indexing lookup when available, coercing the index to the required index type and retargeting obligation spans, otherwise probing for a nearly applicable `Index` impl with unsatisfied predicates, and finally emitting specialized diagnostics for non-indexable types such as tuples or pointers. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `lookup_indexing`, `point_at_index`, and `find_and_report_unsatisfied_index_impl`.

When normal indexing lookup fails, probes for exactly one relevant `Index` impl, instantiates it in a speculative obligation context, equates its self type with the base type, registers and selects its predicates/projection obligations, and reports fulfillment errors if only nested obligations are preventing the impl from applying. It does not call other listed methods.

Post-processes fulfillment errors from indexing so diagnostics point at the index expression span, tracking `Index`/`SliceIndex`-related predicates to retarget only the relevant obligations without duplicating unrelated diagnostics. It does not call other listed methods.

Checks a `yield` expression against the current coroutine context. If coroutine types are available, it calls `check_expr_coercible_to_type` to coerce the yielded value to the coroutine's `yield_ty` and returns the coroutine `resume_ty`. Otherwise it emits an error through `dcx().emit_err`, calls `check_expr` on the yielded value to ensure it is still type-checked, and returns `unit`.

Checks one inline-assembly operand, using `check_expr_with_needs` to type-check the expression with either no place requirement for inputs or mutable-place requirement for outputs, then `require_type_is_sized` to enforce `Sized`. For non-inputs it rejects non-place expressions via `dcx().struct_span_err(...).emit()`. For inputs it calls `structurally_resolve_type` and, when the resolved type is a function item or reference, uses `demand_coerce` to coerce it respectively to a function pointer or raw pointer.

Checks an entire inline `asm!` expression and determines whether it yields `!` or `()`. It calls `check_expr_asm_operand` for each input/output operand, and for label operands it calls `check_block_with_expected` with unit expectation, then uses `demand_suptype` to require `()` when the label block does not diverge. It also restores divergence tracking for label blocks and returns `never` if the asm is guaranteed not to return, otherwise `unit`.

Checks an `offset_of` expression by lowering the container type with `lower_ty`, repeatedly resolving the current container with `structurally_resolve_type`, and walking the requested field path while validating enum variants, tuple fields, and struct fields. Along the way it emits feature and lookup diagnostics, calls `require_type_is_sized` for field types and `require_type_has_static_alignment` for the overall container, checks field visibility/stability, and accumulates the resolved field indices for the final offset computation.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::us: Returns the set of trait imports recorded as used for the item’s type-checking results. It explicitly calls `typeck` to obtain the `TypeckResults` and then reads `used_trait_imports` from them.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::ty: Builds the normal type-checking query for a local item by creating a fallback type from `tcx.type_of(def_id.to_def_id()).instantiate_identity()`. It explicitly calls `typeck_with_fallback` to perform the shared type-checking implementation.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::di: Builds a diagnostic-only type-checking query whose fallback type is an explicit error type tied to the item span. It explicitly calls `typeck_with_fallback` to reuse the common type-checking pipeline.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::in: Runs type checking with an obligation inspector attached, using the item’s declared type as fallback via `tcx.type_of(...).instantiate_identity()`. It explicitly calls `typeck_with_fallback` to execute the shared implementation.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::ty: Implements the core HIR type-checking flow for a body: it redirects closure-like items to their root owner, prepares the root/type inference contexts, locates the body, and type-checks either a function body or a const/static-style body using the provided fallback type. It explicitly calls `typeck` when the current item reuses another item’s root type-check results, and explicitly calls `infer_type_if_missing` to synthesize expected types for non-function bodies before continuing with ABI checking, function checking, coercion checking, fallback, and obligation processing.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::in: Infers an expected type when the HIR item omitted one, handling `_` types, associated consts in impls, `typeof` anonymous consts, and inline/global asm constant or symbol operands. It does not explicitly call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::im: Converts a HIR mutability flag into the corresponding `Needs` value, yielding `MutPlace` for mutable and `None` otherwise. It does not explicitly call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Looks up a required enclosing breakable context by `HirId` and bugs if none exists. It explicitly calls `opt_find_breakable` to perform the actual lookup.
Performs an optional lookup of an enclosing breakable context by `HirId` using the internal id-to-stack index map. It does not explicitly call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::re: Emits an error describing that a resolved path was not the expected kind of variant-like item, with a specialized message for function calls used in patterns. It does not explicitly call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::fa: Constructs and emits an intentional internal compiler bug diagnostic with version and flag information, then diverges. It does not explicitly call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/lib.rs::pr: Registers this crate’s query providers by first delegating method-related provider setup and then overriding the type-checking queries in the shared provider table. It does not explicitly call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/wf: Returns the underlying `ObligationCtxt` by dereferencing `WfCheckingCtxt`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context inside the obligation context; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Normalizes a type-foldable value under the current parameter environment, attaching a `WellFormed` obligation cause for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds and registers a `WellFormed` predicate obligation for a generic argument using the current body and parameter environment. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`.

Creates the temporary inference/obligation context used for well-formedness checking, runs the supplied checker closure, solves obligations, computes implied bounds, lints redundant lifetimes, and resolves/report regions with a compatibility path for some implied-bounds cases; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Top-level dispatcher that selects the appropriate WF checker for the HIR node kind and then checks each generic parameter. It calls `check_item`, `check_trait_item`, `check_impl_item`, `check_foreign_item`, `check_item_type`, and `check_param_wf`.

Checks item-level well-formedness after precollecting item types, handling impls, functions, statics/consts/type aliases, ADTs, and traits according to item kind. It calls `check_impl`, `check_item_fn`, `check_item_type`, `check_type_defn`, and `check_trait`.
Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.

Checks a trait item by precollecting its types, diagnosing misuse of the trait name as an unboxed self trait object, validating the associated item itself, and also validating synthesized associated types for RPITIT methods. It calls `check_dyn_incompatible_self_trait_by_name` and `check_associated_item`.

Analyzes generic associated types across all associated items of a trait to infer potentially missing outlives bounds by repeatedly intersecting constraints discovered from method signatures and other bounds. It calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive`.

Extends a parameter environment with additional clause predicates, returning the original environment unchanged when no new predicates are provided; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Collects GAT arguments appearing in a type/signature and derives required outlives clauses by checking whether referenced types or regions are known to outlive each region argument. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit`, `ty_known_to_outlive`, and `region_known_to_outlive`.
Tests whether a type is known to outlive a region under the current environment by creating a region obligation probe. It calls `test_region_obligations`.
Tests whether one region is known to outlive another under the current environment by probing a subregion constraint. It calls `test_region_obligations`.

Creates a fresh inference context, applies a caller-provided set of region constraints, derives implied bounds from assumed well-formed types, and returns whether region solving succeeds without errors; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Constructs a `GATArgsCollector`, walks a type-foldable value, and returns the non-bound region and type arguments used at the target GAT projection. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit_ty` indirectly through the visitor traversal.
Visitor hook that records lifetime and type arguments from projections of the targeted GAT, then continues recursively through nested types; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Returns whether a HIR type syntactically looks like a single-segment trait object naming the enclosing trait, indicating it may have meant `Self`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks whether a trait item mistakenly refers to its own trait name where `Self` is intended, and emits a suggestion-based diagnostic when this makes the trait non-object-safe. It calls `could_be_self` to detect suspicious type references in associated const/type/function signatures and calls `is_object_safe` to skip diagnostics for object-safe traits.

Checks an impl item after precollecting its types, choosing an appropriate diagnostic span for methods and associated types before delegating to associated-item WF checking. It calls `check_associated_item`.

Checks generic-parameter well-formedness, focusing on const parameters: it either enforces the relevant lang-item trait bound in a WF context on feature-enabled paths or emits structural-match style diagnostics on stable paths. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt` and contains the local helper `ty_is_local`.
Local helper used by `check_param_wf` to decide whether a const-parameter type is local by recursively inspecting ADTs, arrays, slices, shared references, and tuples. It calls itself recursively.

Runs WF checking for an associated const, function, or type inside a dedicated context, ensuring trait coherence first, computing the appropriate `Self` type, and then validating the item-specific signature or value/type. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_associated_type_bounds`.

Checks structs, unions, and enums for representability and field/type well-formedness, enforces `Sized` where required for non-tail fields or packed/drop-sensitive layouts, registers extra obligations such as const evaluatability, and validates where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks a trait item by rejecting associated items on marker traits, validating the trait's where-clauses in a WF context, and then running the GAT missing-bound analysis for real traits. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `check_where_clauses`, and `check_gat_where_clauses`.

Validates explicit bounds on a trait associated type by normalizing each bound, expanding it into clause well-formedness obligations, and registering those obligations. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx` and `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`.
Checks a free or foreign function signature inside a dedicated WF context using the instantiated function signature. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`.

Checks the declared type of an item in a WF context by normalizing it, registering its well-formedness, optionally enforcing `Sized` depending on unsized-handling rules, and requiring `Sync` for eligible shared statics. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.

Checks an impl in a WF context by validating either the implemented trait reference and its derived obligations or the inherent self type, then validating the impl's where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks where-clauses and generic defaults for well-formedness by registering obligations for concrete default types/consts, examining predicate dependencies, normalizing predicates, and feeding the resulting obligations into the current WF context. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.
Visits a type, records the index of any `ty::Param` encountered in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.
Stops traversal when a region is encountered by immediately returning `ControlFlow::Break(())`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Visits a const, records the index of any const generic parameter found in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.

Well-formedness-checks a function or method signature by liberating late-bound regions, normalizing each input/output type with per-parameter locations, registering WF obligations for every input/output type, and checking where-clauses. It explicitly calls `check_where_clauses` and uses `register_bound` to enforce the tuple and `Sized` requirements for `Abi::RustCall` arguments.

Validates a method's `self` receiver by normalizing the method signature, `self_ty`, and receiver type, then checking receiver legality. It explicitly calls `receiver_is_valid`, potentially multiple times under different feature configurations, to decide whether the receiver is accepted or which diagnostic to emit.

Determines whether a method receiver type is valid for a given `Self` type by first trying direct type equality, then autodereferencing toward `self_ty`, registering autoderef obligations on success. When arbitrary self types are not enabled, it explicitly calls `receiver_is_implemented` at each deref step and also registers the corresponding `Receiver` bound before continuing.

Checks whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the `Receiver` lang-item trait by building the trait obligation and testing it with `predicate_must_hold_modulo_regions`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Checks that generic parameters of an ADT or lazy type alias are sufficiently constrained for variance computation, skipping items whose field/alias types already contain errors. It explicitly calls `identify_constrained_generic_params` to extend the constrained set and `report_bivariance` to emit diagnostics for unconstrained parameters.

Builds and emits the diagnostic for an unused/bivariant generic parameter, selecting item-specific help text and collecting spans where the parameter or `Self` alias appears. It explicitly calls `IsProbablyCyclical::visit_def` to detect likely recursive ADTs/type aliases so it can report recursive-usage diagnostics instead of plain unused-parameter errors.

Finds elaborated predicates on the current item that are globally true but nontrivial, normalizes them, refines their source span to the matching predicate clause when possible, and registers them as `TrivialBound` obligations. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

Runs well-formedness checking over all items, impl items, trait items, foreign items, and opaques in a module in parallel, combining their results, and checks for the crate entry function at the crate root. It explicitly calls `check_well_formed` for each covered definition.

Computes candidate lifetimes for an item, including late-bound function lifetimes when relevant, and uses the outlives environment to detect and lint lifetime parameters that are redundant because they are equivalent to an earlier lifetime. It does not call other methods from the provided list.
Registers this module's query providers by installing `check_mod_type_wf` and `check_well_formed` into the compiler provider table. It explicitly references `check_mod_type_wf` from the methods list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/fn_ctxt/mo: Constructs a fresh `FnCtxt` for a body, initializing inference-related state, divergence tracking, breakable-scope storage, and links to the shared root context. It explicitly calls `parse_never_type_options_attr` to compute never-type fallback and diverging-block behavior.
Returns the diagnostic context from the enclosing type context by calling `tcx.dcx()`.
Builds an `ObligationCause` for the current body and span. It explicitly calls `ObligationCause::new`.
Creates a generic miscellaneous obligation cause for a span. It explicitly calls `cause` with `ObligationCauseCode::Misc`.
Returns the compiler `Session` stored in the type context.

Builds a `TypeErrCtxt` for rich diagnostics, seeding subtype-constraint data from pending obligations and wiring closures for function-signature normalization and autoderef exploration. It explicitly calls `add_constraints`, `pending_obligations`, `probe`, `normalize`, `select_all_or_error`, `resolve_vars_if_possible`, `autoderef`, `silence_errors`, `next`, and `current_obligations`.
Dereferences `FnCtxt` to its underlying `TypeckRootCtxt` by returning `root_ctxt`.
Returns the `TyCtxt` used by this lowering context.
Returns the current body's `DefId`. It explicitly calls `to_def_id` on `body_id`.
Indicates that type lowering inside bodies is allowed to create inference variables by always returning `true`.
Creates a fresh region inference variable for a lowered lifetime, using either a parameter-based or miscellaneous origin. It explicitly calls `next_region_var`.
Creates a fresh type inference variable, reusing a generic-parameter-backed variable when available. It explicitly calls `var_for_def`, `as_type`, `unwrap`, and `next_ty_var`.

Creates a fresh const inference variable, with special handling for host-effect const parameters and generic const parameters. It explicitly calls `var_for_effect`, `as_const`, `unwrap`, `var_for_def`, and `next_const_var`.

Synthesizes visible trait bounds for a local type parameter by filtering the current `ParamEnv` caller bounds to predicates whose self type is that parameter. It explicitly calls `hir`, `ty_param_owner`, `generics_of`, `to_def_id`, `def_span`, `caller_bounds`, `kind`, `skip_binder`, `self_ty`, and `is_param`.

Lowers an associated type projection by instantiating the trait reference with fresh inference variables, lowering the associated item's generic arguments, and constructing the projection type. It explicitly calls `instantiate_binder_with_fresh_vars`, `lowerer`, `lower_generic_args_of_assoc_item`, `tcx`, and `new_projection`.

Attempts to recover an ADT definition from a type, returning direct ADTs immediately and normalizing projection/inherent/weak aliases before retrying. It explicitly calls `kind`, `has_escaping_bound_vars`, `normalize`, and `ty_adt_def`.

Records the lowered type for a HIR node, first adding better-caused obligations for projection/weak aliases and normalizing when the type has no escaping bound vars. It explicitly calls `has_escaping_bound_vars`, `kind`, `add_required_obligations_for_hir`, `normalize`, and `write_ty`.
Exposes the underlying inference context by returning `Some(&self.infcx)`.
Marks the inference context as tainted by an emitted error. It explicitly calls `set_tainted_by_errors` on `infcx`.

Builds a `LoweredTy` from a raw type by computing a normalized/resolved form appropriate to the active trait solver. It explicitly calls `next_trait_solver`, and then either `try_structurally_resolve_type` or `normalize`.

Parses the crate-level `rustc_never_type_options` attribute, validating `fallback` and `diverging_block_default` entries, reporting malformed or duplicate options, and filling in defaults from feature flags. It explicitly calls `get_attr`, `meta_item_list`, `value_str`, `dcx`, `span_err`, `span`, `name_or_empty`, and `features`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Constructs an early-bound `ResolvedArg` for a generic parameter and returns it paired with the parameter's local def-id; it calls `to_def_id` to convert the local id for `ResolvedArg::EarlyBound`.

Constructs an innermost late-bound `ResolvedArg` for a generic parameter at the given index and returns it paired with the parameter's local def-id; it calls `to_def_id` to build `ResolvedArg::LateBound`.
Returns the underlying `DefId` for early-bound, late-bound, and free resolved arguments, and `None` for `StaticLifetime` or `Error`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Shifts the De Bruijn depth of a late-bound argument by the given amount and leaves other variants unchanged; for `ResolvedArg::LateBound` it calls `shifted_in` on the depth.
Formats each `Scope` variant in a truncated debug form that omits recursive scope tails; it calls the formatter builder methods `debug_struct`, `field`, and `finish`.

Registers this module's query providers, wiring `resolve_bound_vars`, `is_late_bound_map`, `object_lifetime_default`, and closure-based accessors for stored maps; the accessors call `tcx.resolve_bound_vars(id)` and then `get` on the resulting maps.

Builds the `ResolveBoundVars` result for one HIR owner by creating a `BoundVarContext`, dispatching to the matching visitor entry point, and then copying collected definitions into owner-indexed maps. It calls `hir_owner_node`, then one of `visit_item`, `visit_foreign_item`, `visit_trait_item`, or `visit_impl_item`, and finally uses `entry`, `or_default`, and `insert` to populate the result.

Converts a `ResolvedArg::LateBound` plus its generic parameter into the corresponding `ty::BoundVariableKind`, using the parameter kind to choose region, type, or const binding. It calls `hir`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `expect_local`, and `name` to recover the bound variable's HIR name.

Walks outward through the current scope stack to determine the binder variables and binder composition mode for a nested poly-trait-ref, including concatenating enclosing binder vars with supertrait vars when needed. It calls `clone`, `is_empty`, `dcx`, `delayed_bug`, `entry`, `or_default`, and `extend`.

Processes a poly trait reference by computing enclosing binder context, creating late-bound entries for its bound generic parameters, optionally rejecting non-lifetime binders, recording the resulting binder list, and visiting the trait ref inside a new binder scope. It calls `poly_trait_ref_binder_info`, `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `insert`, `extend`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, and `visit_trait_ref`.
Returns the HIR map used for nested visiting; it calls `hir` on the type context.
Visits a nested body within a `Body` scope so inner references resolve with the body boundary in place. It calls `hir`, `body`, `with`, `id`, and `visit_body`.

Handles closure expressions specially: it diagnoses inferred types inside `for<>` closures, builds late-bound vars for closure binders, rejects non-region late-bound params, records the binders, and then visits the closure within a new binder scope; non-closure expressions are walked normally. It calls the local helper `span_of_infer`, then `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, and `walk_expr`.
Local helper for `visit_expr` that searches a type for an inferred `_` and returns its span if found. It calls the nested visitor's `visit_ty` and then `break_value` on the control-flow result.
Walks a type looking for `hir::TyKind::Infer`, returning `Break(span)` when found and otherwise recursing. It calls `walk_ty` for non-infer subtrees.

Dispatches item handling based on item kind: records empty late-bound vars for trait impl refs, uses `visit_early_late` for functions, walks items with no lifetime parameters directly, gives opaque types a parent-aware root plus binder and trait-ref-boundary scopes, and uses early-binding handling for other generic items. It calls `record_late_bound_vars`, `visit_early_late`, `walk_item`, `ResolvedArg::early`, `insert`, `with`, and `visit_early`.

Validates and resolves a precise capture argument, accepting lifetime params and type/const params, rejecting invalid captures, and emitting specialized diagnostics for bad self-alias captures. It calls `resolve_lifetime_ref`, `dcx`, `emit_err`, `resolve_type_ref`, `expect_local`, `def_span`, `def_descr`, `descr`, and `to_string`.
Handles foreign items by using `visit_early_late` for foreign functions and otherwise just walking foreign statics and types. It calls `visit_early_late` and `walk_foreign_item`.

Resolves bindings inside types, with special handling for bare function types, trait objects, explicit lifetime parameters, references, and opaque defs. It builds and records late-bound vars for bare fns, visits trait-object bounds under a trait-ref boundary, applies object lifetime defaulting or normal lifetime visiting, and performs additional opaque-type validation. It calls `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, `walk_ty`, `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`, `resolve_object_lifetime_default`, and `visit_lifetime`.
Visits a pattern-type pattern by delegating to the standard pattern walker; it calls `walk_pat`.

Handles trait items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_trait_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, `visit_param_bound`, and `visit_ty`.

Handles impl items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_impl_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, and `visit_ty`.

Resolves a lifetime reference according to its kind: inserts `'static`, resolves named lifetime params, and ignores error or inference/default placeholders for later stages. It calls `insert_lifetime` for `Static` and `resolve_lifetime_ref` for `Param`.

Visits each path segment's generic arguments with the correct depth and resolves paths that refer to type or const parameters. It calls `visit_segment_args` for segment arguments and `resolve_type_ref` on type/const parameter paths.

Processes a function-like item by extracting the output type, copying inferred-delegation late-bound vars when present, applying lifetime elision analysis, walking the function signature/kind, and then visiting the body. It calls `fn_sig`, `skip_binder`, `bound_vars`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `visit_fn_like_elision`, `walk_fn_kind`, and `visit_nested_body`.
Visits generic parameters and where predicates inside a trait-ref-boundary scope so nested trait refs are resolved with the proper boundary. It calls `with`.

Resolves where-predicates by creating a binder scope for bound predicates, recording their late-bound vars, and then visiting the bounded type and bounds; region predicates visit the lifetime and bounds, while equality predicates visit both sides. It calls `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, `visit_ty`, and `visit_lifetime`.
Visits a poly trait ref using the general inner handler with non-lifetime binders allowed; it calls `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`.
Visits an anonymous const under a late-boundary scope so late-bound regions cannot escape into constants. It calls `with` and `walk_anon_const`.

Resolves type and const generic parameters as references to themselves, then visits any default type, const type, or const default body attached to the parameter. It calls `resolve_type_ref`, `visit_ty`, `hir`, `body`, and `visit_body`.

Computes the object lifetime default for a type parameter by inspecting its HIR generics and collecting direct `T: 'a` outlives bounds. It queries HIR/generics metadata via `hir_node_by_def_id`, `local_parent`, `hir`, `get_generics`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, and `bounds_for_param`, and returns `Empty`, `Static`, `Param`, or `Ambiguous` depending on the collected lifetime set.
Creates a nested `BoundVarContext` with a replacement scope and executes a callback inside that scope. It enters a debug span with `enter` and then invokes the provided closure `f`.
Stores the late-bound variable binder list for a HIR node in the output map and rejects accidental overwrites. It updates the map with `insert`.

Builds a binder scope where lifetime params may be early- or late-bound depending on `tcx.is_late_bound`, records the resulting late-bound binder kinds, and visits the nested item in that scope. It calls `record_late_bound_vars` to save binder info and `with` to traverse under the constructed `Scope::Binder`.

Builds a binder scope where all generic parameters are treated as early-bound, records that there are no late-bound vars, and then visits the nested item under both a binder scope and a trait-ref boundary. It calls `record_late_bound_vars` and uses `with` twice to install the scopes.

Resolves a lifetime reference by walking outward through the scope stack, tracking De Bruijn depth, root generics, binder entries, body ownership, and late-bound capture barriers to classify the reference as early-bound, late-bound, free, error, or unresolved. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, `get_generics`, and `shifted` while traversing scopes, and emits diagnostics through `feature_err`, `emit`, and `emit_err` when fresh/elided or improperly captured lifetimes are encountered.

Resolves a type or const generic parameter reference by walking outward through scopes, tracking binder depth and late-bound capture barriers, and classifying the reference as early-bound, late-bound, or unresolved/error. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, and `shifted` during lookup, and emits capture diagnostics with `emit_err` before recording the final result with `insert`.

Visits generic arguments on a path segment, resolving explicit lifetimes first, handling paren-sugar function traits specially, and computing object-lifetime-default scopes for type arguments based on the referenced item and surrounding context. It explicitly calls `visit_fn_like_elision` for paren-sugar segments, `visit_lifetime` for lifetime args, `object_lifetime_default` to compute defaults for type parameters, `with` to enter object-default scopes, `visit_ty` for type args, `visit_anon_const` for const args, `visit_id` for inferred args, and `supertrait_hrtb_vars` when collecting higher-ranked vars from supertraits.

Searches a trait/supertrait graph for an associated item with the given name and kind, accumulating higher-ranked bound variables introduced by traversed supertrait predicates. It queries associated items with `associated_items`/`find_by_name_and_kind`, fetches relevant supertrait predicates with `super_predicates_that_define_assoc_item`, and extends the traversal stack with collected obligations.

Visits function-like input/output types under an object-lifetime-default scope that supplies `'static` for elided trait-object lifetimes, except that closure outputs are visited outside that scope. It calls `with` to install the defaulting scope and `visit_ty` to traverse input and output types.

Resolves an elided object lifetime by scanning outward for the nearest applicable object-lifetime-default scope, adjusting for intervening binders, and defaulting to `'static` at the root. It calls `insert_lifetime` to record the chosen lifetime after applying `shifted`.
Records the resolved lifetime for a lifetime HIR node in the output map. It updates the definitions table with `insert`.

Removes a previously inserted lifetime mapping when later validation determines that the resolution was erroneous, asserting that the removed value matches the expected bad definition. It removes the entry with `swap_remove`.

Computes the set of lifetime parameters in a function owner that should be treated as late-bound by comparing where each lifetime appears in inputs, outputs, and where-clauses, while excluding lifetimes constrained through type aliases after lowering. It drives analysis by calling HIR accessors such as `fn_decl_by_hir_id` and `get_generics`, invokes the nested collectors via `visit_ty`, `walk_fn_ret_ty`, and `visit_generics`, and finally allocates the resulting set with `alloc`.
